sources.title: Congreso aprueba norma que atenta contra el derecho de las personas trans a usar baños públicos - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the Congress's Women and Family Commission approved unanimously the dictamen of bills 6506/2023-CR (Montoya) and 8457/2023-CR (Muñante), which prohibit entry to public sanitary services designated to the opposite sex at birth (exceptions: custody, medical attention, accompanying a person under 12, an elderly person or a person with a disability) and prohibit ambiguous bathroom signage; the dictamen still required plenary support. Context: in July 2023 a complaint about the gendered signage at Jorge Chávez International Airport led to the labels being changed to 'mujeres/hombres en su diversidad'. Activist Gianna Camacho states no official statistics of trans violence in women's bathrooms exist, and enforcement would rest on individual security staff judging IDs.

sources.title: Discriminación legalizada: sobre la prohibición del Congreso a personas trans para acceder a baños públicos - IDEHPUCP
sources.claim_summary: IDEHPUCP bulletin, analysis by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte (15 Apr 2025): on Wednesday 2 April 2025 the Plenary of Congress approved, exempting it from a second vote, the dictamen of the law strengthening the right to the sexual indemnity of children and adolescents (merger of bills 6505/2023-CR and 8457/2023-CR). Article 5.1 of the bill bans entry and use of public sanitary services to any person whose biological sex does not match the service's designated sex, with narrow exceptions for accompaniment/assistance and legal or judicial mandates. The bulletin reads the provision as a direct violation of equality and non-discrimination (Political Constitution art. 2.2, American Convention art. 1.1) in line with IACtHR OC-24/17, and as validating stereotypes about trans people.

sources.title: Perú: aumentaron los crímenes de odio y las mujeres trans son las más afectadas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Agencia Presentes (22 Jul 2024) on the Annual Report of the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of the Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia: 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023; more than half the homicide victims were trans women (30), then gay men (23) and one lesbian woman; yearly homicides 2020: 12 (8 trans women), 2021: 10, 2022: 13, 2023: 19 (12 trans women). Killings involved extreme cruelty (multiple gunshots, stabblings, throat-cuttings); rights violations peaked at 61 in 2020 (43 in 2022, 34 in 2023, 32 in 2021), trans women again the most affected. Includes testimony that in Feb 2023 extortion gang 'Los Gallegos' abducted sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano (31) in central Lima and killed her in Carabayllo with ~30 shots, a case of the pimping-mafia violence the movement identifies as the main trans-femicide driver.
